subtopics.name: External Factors that Impact Business Decisions

parts.problem_md: Define the term **external factor**
parts.solution_md:
> **[mark-scheme]**
> - Something outside of a business's control that can affect its decisions and performance **[1 mark]**
> 
> Award 1 mark for a correct definition of **external factor**.
> 
> Alternative acceptable answers:
> 
> - A force in the business environment that a company cannot directly influence but must respond to

> **[exam-tip]**
> When defining a term, make sure your answer captures two key elements: what the thing *is* and what it *does*. For "external factor", you need to show that it is outside the business's control and that it has an impact on the business. A common mistake is only stating one of these elements, e.g. just saying "something that affects a business" without mentioning that it is beyond the business's control.

**[1 mark]**

parts.problem_md:
> **[case-study]**
> *The Better Toy Store (TBTS)* is a children’s toy shop. *TBTS *has three shops in Singapore. Two of the shops are located in busy shopping malls and the third is located at the Jewel Changi Airport. *TBTS *has a website for customers looking to buy toys online.
> 
> *TBTS *selects toys to sell that are excellent for play, value, design and quality. All *TBTS *toys are environmentally friendly.

State **one **factor *TBTS* should consider when selecting its manufacturers.
parts.solution_md:
> **[mark-scheme]**
> - Whether the manufacturer uses environmentally friendly materials and processes in toy production **[1 mark]**
> 
> OR
> 
> - Whether the manufacturer can produce toys that meet TBTS's standards for quality and design **[1 mark]**
> 
> OR
> 
> - Whether the manufacturer can offer competitive prices so that TBTS can provide good value to its customers **[1 mark]**
> 
> OR
> 
> - Any other appropriate response in the context of TBTS **[1 mark]**
> 
> Award 1 mark for a relevant factor the business should consider when selecting its manufacturers in the context of TBTS
> 
> Marks are not awarded for a factor that is not in the context of TBTS

> **[exam-tip]**
> Make sure your answer is linked to the context of TBTS. Think about what makes TBTS distinctive — e.g. its focus on environmentally friendly toys, quality, design and value. A generic answer such as "cost" without linking it to TBTS's specific priorities is unlikely to earn the mark. Always refer back to the extract to find clues about what the business values.

**[1 mark]**

parts.problem_md:
> **[case-study]**
> *Nantgwynfaen Organic Farm (NOF)* is a farm growing a range of fruit and vegetables. It has a farm shop and offers accommodation with breakfast. It was set up by Amanda and Ken Edwards in West Wales, UK.
> 
> *NOF *supports farmers by selling local organic produce in its farm shop. The produce from the farm shop is served to the visitors staying overnight at the farm.
> 
> *NOF *is committed to being environmentally friendly by recycling, avoiding the use of packaging and reducing the use of electricity.
> 
> The demand for *NOF* products can be affected by external factors.

State **one **external factor that could cause a change in demand for *NOF *products.
parts.solution_md:
> **[mark-scheme]**
> Any 1 from:
> 
> - A change in demand patterns could lead to people buying more organic farmed produce **[1 mark]**
> 
> OR
> 
> - A change in weather/climate that affects the growing season for fruit and vegetables **[1 mark]**
> 
> OR
> 
> - New government legislation on food labelling or organic standards **[1 mark]**
> 
> OR
> 
> - Any other appropriate external factor in the context of NOF **[1 mark]**
> 
> Award 1 mark for an appropriate external factor that could cause a change in demand, in the context of Nantgwynfaen Organic Farm
> 
> Marks are not awarded for a factor that is not in the context of Nantgwynfaen Organic Farm

> **[exam-tip]**
> Make sure the factor you identify is genuinely external — that is, something outside the control of the business, such as changes in the economy, weather, legislation or consumer trends. A common mistake is to give an internal factor (e.g. changing the prices in the farm shop), which would not be credited. Always link your answer back to the context of NOF to show the examiner you understand how the factor applies to this specific business.

**[1 mark]**

parts.problem_md:
> **[case-study]**
> *TechBrew Coffee* was founded in 2020 by Marcus Chen in the bustling Shoreditch area of London. *TechBrew Coffee*'s mission is to provide 'an innovative café experience where customers can enjoy expertly crafted coffee while exploring the latest digital tools and attending our regular technology workshops.'
> 
> *TechBrew Coffee* offers a range of services including its popular Weekend Coding Club where customers can learn basic programming skills. The café also runs Corporate Innovation Sessions and After-School Robotics Classes for children. Customers can purchase tech accessories and specialty coffee beans from the shop.
> 
> *TechBrew Coffee* is a profit-making organisation with a community focus. It employs fifteen staff, a mix of full-time and part-time workers, many of whom live in the local area.

Which **one** of the following is a technological factor that can affect a business?

Select **one** answer
parts.solution_md:
**The correct answer is D**

Automation in production is a technological factor because it relates to advances in technology and innovation that can change how a business operates, produces goods, or delivers services.

**A** is incorrect as an ageing population is a social/demographic factor

**B** is incorrect as changes in exchange rates is an economic factor

**C** is incorrect as new environmental regulations is a political/legal factor

parts.problem_md:
> **[case-study]**
> *Artify Studio* was set up in 2015 by Tay Hui Jae in the busy Kampong Glam area of Singapore. *Artify Studio*’s aim is to have ‘a communal art space where people can come together and paint, where people would be given as much creative freedom as they would have if they were in their own spaces.’
> 
> *Artify Studio* provides many services including its popular Liberty Art Jam where customers can paint as well as listen to music. The studio offers a Corporate Art Jam and Regular Kids Classes. Customers can purchase art materials after attending the studio.* *
> 
> *Artify Studio* is a profit-making organisation with a social element. It employs seven part-time people, all of whom are art enthusiasts.

Which **one **of the following is a political factor that can affect a business?

Select **one **answer
parts.solution_md:
**The correct answer is A**

Taxation is a political factor because it is determined by government policy and directly affects how businesses operate and their profitability.

**B** is incorrect as global warming is an environmental factor

**C** is incorrect as habitat destruction is an environmental factor

**D** is incorrect as part-time workers is a social or economic factor

parts.problem_md:
> **[case-study]**
> Drift is a small ice cream business based on the island of Rügen, Germany. It sells handmade ice cream from a van on the beach during the summer months. The owner, Lukas, has noticed that summers on Rügen have become hotter and longer over the past five years.

Outline one way an environmental factor could affect Drift
parts.solution_md:
Hotter and longer summers on Rügen could extend Drift's selling season **[1 mark]**

This means Lukas has more days to trade from the beach, which could increase the business's annual revenue **[1 mark]**

> **[mark-scheme]**
> Award 1 mark for identifying one way an environmental factor could affect Drift
> 
> Award 1 further mark for outlining it in the context of the business
> 
> Alternative answers:
> 
> - Rising temperatures could increase demand for ice cream **[1 mark]**. From tourists visiting the island, this would allow Lukas to sell more each day, boosting daily takings during the summer months **[1 mark]**
> - Increasing concern about the environment could lead customers to expect Drift to use recyclable or biodegradable packaging **[1 mark]**. If Lukas does not adapt, customers may choose to buy from a competitor who does, reducing sales **[1 mark]**
> - Accept any other appropriate response

> **[exam-tip]**
> The command word "outline" means you need to identify a relevant point and then develop it briefly. Make sure you go beyond simply naming an environmental factor — you must link it to a specific effect on Drift. Many students lose the second mark by keeping their answer too general (e.g. "climate change could affect the business"). Instead, explain how the factor impacts something specific such as revenue, demand or costs, and try to refer to details from the extract to show context.

**[2 marks]**

parts.problem_md:
> **[case-study]**
> *GreenLeaf Café* was established in 2018 by Priya Sharma in the vibrant Shoreditch area of London. *GreenLeaf Café*'s mission is to provide 'a welcoming space where people can enjoy plant-based food and drinks in a relaxed, community-focused environment.'
> 
> *GreenLeaf Café* offers a range of services including its popular Weekend Brunch Menu, Corporate Catering packages and Weekly Cooking Workshops. Customers can also purchase recipe books and branded merchandise from the café.
> 
> *GreenLeaf Café* is a small private limited company that employs twelve staff, a mix of full-time and part-time workers, all of whom are passionate about sustainable living.

Which **one** of the following is a legal factor that can affect a business?

Select **one** answer
parts.solution_md:
**The correct answer is B**

Minimum wage legislation is a legal factor because it is a law set by the government that businesses must comply with, directly affecting their costs and how they manage employees.

**A** is incorrect as rising unemployment is an economic factor

**C** is incorrect as an ageing population is a social factor

**D** is incorrect as the use of automation is a technological factor

parts.problem_md:
> **[case-study]**
> Relay is a small courier business based in Seoul, South Korea. The owner, Ji-hoon, employs ten drivers who deliver parcels across the city using petrol-powered vans. The South Korean government has recently announced plans to ban petrol vehicles from the city centre within the next five years.

Outline one way this political factor could affect Relay
parts.solution_md:
> **[mark-scheme]**
> Award 1 mark for identifying one way the political factor could affect Relay and 1 further mark for outlining it in the context of the business
> 
> "Outline" requires a brief description that shows understanding of the impact, applied to the business context
> 
> Any pair from (1 mark per point):
> 
> - The ban on petrol vehicles would mean Ji-hoon has to replace his fleet with electric vans **[1 mark]**
> - This would require significant investment, increasing the business's costs **[1 mark]**
> 
> OR
> 
> - The planned ban could cause Relay to lose customers in the city centre if it cannot deliver there **[1 mark]**
> - This would reduce revenue from one of Seoul's busiest areas for parcel deliveries **[1 mark]**
> 
> OR
> 
> - The government announcement may encourage Ji-hoon to start switching to electric vehicles now before the deadline **[1 mark]**
> - This would allow Relay to spread the cost over five years rather than replacing all ten vans at once **[1 mark]**
> 
> OR
> 
> - Accept any other appropriate response
> 
> **[2 marks]**
> 
> 1 mark for identifying a relevant way the political factor could affect Relay and 1 mark for the correctly linked outline in the context of the business

> **[exam-tip]**
> Make sure you link your answer specifically to Relay and the details in the extract, such as the petrol-powered vans, the ten drivers or the five-year deadline. A generic answer about political factors affecting businesses will not earn the second mark. The command word "outline" means you need to go beyond simply identifying the impact — you should briefly develop your point to show how or why it affects the business.

**[2 marks]**

parts.problem_md:
> **[case-study]**
> *GreenLeaf Bakery* was established in 2018 by Priya Sharma in the vibrant Brick Lane area of London. *GreenLeaf Bakery*'s mission is to provide 'a welcoming space where the local community can enjoy freshly baked goods made from locally sourced ingredients, while learning about healthy eating through our regular workshops.'
> 
> *GreenLeaf Bakery* offers a range of services including its popular Weekend Bake Club where customers can learn to bake artisan bread. The bakery also runs Corporate Team-Building Sessions and After-School Baking Classes for children. Customers can purchase baking equipment and ingredients from the shop.
> 
> *GreenLeaf Bakery* is a profit-making organisation with a community focus. It employs twelve staff, a mix of full-time and part-time workers, many of whom live in the local area.

Which **one** of the following is a social factor that can affect a business?

Select **one** answer
parts.solution_md:
**The correct answer is C**

Changes in lifestyle trends is a social factor because it relates to shifts in consumer behaviour and preferences within society, which directly influence the demand for a business's products or services.

**A** is incorrect as interest rates is an economic factor

**B** is incorrect as new legislation is a political/legal factor

**D** is incorrect as automation in production is a technological factor

parts.problem_md: Define the term **environmental factor**.
parts.solution_md:
> **[mark-scheme]**
> - An issue relating to the natural world, such as climate change or pollution, that can affect how a business operates **[1 mark]**
> 
> OR
> 
> - A concern about the physical environment, such as sustainability or waste, that may influence business decisions **[1 mark]**
> 
> Award 1 mark for a correct definition of **environmental factor**.
> 
> "Define" requires a clear, precise statement of meaning.

> **[exam-tip]**
> Make sure your definition links the concept back to the natural/physical world and its impact on business. A common mistake is to confuse environmental factors with other external factors such as economic or political issues. Including a relevant example, such as climate change, pollution or sustainability, can help demonstrate your understanding and make your definition clearer.

**[1 mark]**

parts.problem_md:
> **[case-study]**
> Greenfield Foods is a large food manufacturing company based in the UK. The Managing Director believes that the business has a responsibility to the local community.
> 
> *Greenfield Foods* provides apprenticeship programmes for young people in the area and pays all its workers above the minimum wage. The company also donates a percentage of its profits to local charities and sponsors community events. *Greenfield Foods* sources many of its ingredients from local farmers, supporting small businesses in the region.
> 
> The Managing Director uses regular staff meetings to communicate these social objectives to employees.

Analyse why *Greenfield Foods* would want to be more socially responsible.
parts.solution_md:
Being socially responsible improves Greenfield Foods' reputation with customers and the local community **[1 mark]**. By paying workers above the minimum wage and providing apprenticeships for young people **[1 mark]**, customers may prefer to buy from a company that treats its workers fairly, helping Greenfield Foods to increase sales and build brand loyalty **[1 mark]**

Donating profits to local charities and sponsoring community events helps Greenfield Foods to strengthen its relationship with the local community **[1 mark]**. Supporting local causes and sourcing ingredients from local farmers **[1 mark]** can generate positive publicity and goodwill, making it easier for the business to gain planning permission or local support if it wants to expand its operations in the area **[1 mark]**

> **[mark-scheme]**
> Award up to 2 marks for identifying reasons why Greenfield Foods would want to be more socially responsible
> 
> Up to 2 further marks are awarded for applying the reasons to Greenfield Foods' context
> 
> Up to 2 further marks are awarded for explaining the reasons to the business
> 
> **Alternative ways to answer**
> 
> - Providing apprenticeships and paying above the minimum wage can help Greenfield Foods attract and retain motivated employees **[1 mark]**. Workers who feel valued because of fair pay and training opportunities **[1 mark]** are likely to be more productive and less likely to leave, reducing recruitment and training costs for the business **[1 mark]**
> - Sourcing ingredients from local farmers supports small businesses in the region **[1 mark]**. By building strong relationships with local suppliers **[1 mark]**, Greenfield Foods may benefit from more reliable supply chains and fresher ingredients, which can improve product quality and give the company a competitive advantage **[1 mark]**
> 
> Answers that list six reasons why Greenfield Foods would want to be more socially responsible with no explanation will get a maximum of 1 mark
> 
> No marks are awarded for a definition alone

parts.problem_md:
> **[case-study]**
> *Kraft Heinz* has set itself many targets to reach before 2025. These include reducing its impact on the environment and improving its use of robotic technology for production. It is hoped that these targets will lower the impact *Kraft Heinz* production has on the environment by reducing its waste and greenhouse gases that contribute to global warming.
> 
> **Figure 2 **shows the amount of waste to landfill for *Kraft Heinz* from 2019 to 2021.
> 
> |   | Landfill (metric tons) |
> |---|---|
> | 2019 | 100,595 |
> | 2020 | 92,856 |
> | 2021 | 82,617 |
> 
> **Figure 2**

Calculate the decrease in waste to landfill in metric tons for *Kraft Heinz* from 2019 to 2021. You are advised to show your working.
parts.solution_md:
$=100,595-82,617$ **[1 mark]**

$= 17 , 978  \text{metric tons}$ **[1 mark]**

> **[mark-scheme]**
> Award 1 mark for correctly substituting the numbers into the formula.
> 
> Award 1 mark for the correct answer of **17,978 metric tons**.
> 
> Award full marks for the correct numerical answer without working shown.

> **[exam-tip]**
> Always show your working in calculation questions. Even if you arrive at the wrong final answer, you can still pick up a mark for demonstrating the correct method. Here, the question asks for the "decrease", so you need to subtract the 2021 figure from the 2019 figure. Make sure you read the data from the table carefully and do not mix up the years.

**[2 marks]**

parts.problem_md: Explain one way a social factor could affect a business
parts.solution_md:
A change in population demographics, such as an ageing population, could shift demand towards different products and services **[1 mark]** meaning the business may need to adapt its product range to meet the needs of older customers **[1 mark]** or risk losing sales to competitors who respond to the change more quickly **[1 mark]**

> **[mark-scheme]**
> Award 1 mark for identifying a way a social factor could affect a business
> 
> 2 further marks are awarded for explaining the way, for a maximum of 3 marks
> 
> **Alternative ways to answer**
> 
> - A growing trend towards healthy lifestyles could increase demand for healthier products **[1 mark]** meaning a food business may need to change its ingredients or develop new product lines **[1 mark]** which could increase costs but also attract new customers and boost revenue **[1 mark]**
> - Changes in consumer attitudes towards ethical shopping could affect a business **[1 mark]** as customers may refuse to buy from businesses that do not treat workers fairly **[1 mark]** leading to a fall in sales and damage to the business's reputation **[1 mark]**
> 
> Accept any other appropriate response
> 
> Answers that list three ways a social factor could affect a business will get a maximum of 1 mark
> 
> No marks are awarded for a definition alone

parts.problem_md:
> **[case-study]**
> *The Better Toy Store (TBTS)* is a children’s toy shop. *TBTS *has three shops in Singapore. Two of the shops are located in busy shopping malls and the third is located at the Jewel Changi Airport. *TBTS *has a website for customers looking to buy toys online.
> 
> *TBTS *selects toys to sell that are excellent for play, value, design and quality. All *TBTS *toys are environmentally friendly.

Analyse the likely impact of external factors on business decisions made by *TBTS*.
parts.solution_md:
A social trend towards parents wanting educational and environmentally friendly toys for their children could increase demand for TBTS's products **[1 mark]**. Since TBTS already selects toys that are excellent for play and are environmentally friendly **[1 mark]**, the business is well positioned to benefit from this trend, which could lead to higher sales across its three shops in Singapore and through its website **[1 mark]**

Advances in technology could also affect TBTS's business decisions **[1 mark]**. As more customers in Singapore choose to shop online, TBTS may need to invest in improving its website to offer a better experience, such as faster delivery or a wider product range **[1 mark]**. If TBTS does not keep up with technological changes, it could lose customers to online competitors, particularly as it already faces competition from other toy retailers in the busy shopping malls where two of its shops are located **[1 mark]**

> **[mark-scheme]**
> Award up to 2 marks for identifying impacts of external factors on business decisions made by TBTS
> 
> Up to 2 further marks are awarded for applying the impacts to TBTS's context
> 
> Up to 2 further marks are awarded for explaining the impacts to the business
> 
> **Alternative ways to answer**
> 
> - New government regulations on toy safety standards could require TBTS to change the products it stocks **[1 mark]**. TBTS already selects toys based on quality and design **[1 mark]**, but stricter political regulations could limit the range of toys available to sell, reducing customer choice and potentially affecting sales **[1 mark]**
> - Environmental concerns could lead to stricter rules on packaging and plastic use in Singapore **[1 mark]**. TBTS already sells environmentally friendly toys, but it may need to invest in sustainable packaging for online orders sent through its website **[1 mark]**, increasing costs at a time when it is also paying rent on three shop locations including the premium Jewel Changi Airport site **[1 mark]**
> 
> Answers that list six impacts of external factors on business decisions made by TBTS with no explanation will get a maximum of 1 mark
> 
> No marks are awarded for a definition alone

parts.problem_md:
> **[case-study]**
> Saving the environment in which we all live is important. The Chairman ensures that *Emirates *works hard to recycle many of the materials it uses and to reduce atmospheric pollution from the fuel that powers its aircraft. Water consumption for washing aircraft has been reduced, newspapers and other paper products collected from *Emirates *aircraft cabins are recycled. *Emirates* uses a variety of methods to monitor its employees when carrying out these jobs. For these roles *Emirates *uses a short chain of command.
> 
> *Emirates *used 13,457,776 litres of petrol in 2016–2017. In 2017–2018 it reduced this figure by 12.5%.

Calculate the number of litres of petrol that *Emirates *used in 2017–2018. You are advised to show your workings.
parts.solution_md:
**Method 1:**

$13 , 457 , 776 \div 100 \times 12 . 5 = 1 , 682 , 222$ **[1 mark]**

$13 , 457 , 776 - 1 , 682 , 222 = 11 , 775 , 554$ **[1 mark]**

**Method 2:**

$13 , 457 , 776 \times 0 . 125 = 1 , 682 , 222$ **[1 mark]**

$13 , 457 , 776 - 1 , 682 , 222 = 11 , 775 , 554$ **[1 mark]**

Final answer: **11,775,554 litres**

> **[mark-scheme]**
> Award 1 mark for correctly calculating the 12.5% reduction (i.e. substituting numbers into the formula correctly).
> 
> Award 1 mark for subtracting the reduction from the original figure to arrive at the correct answer.
> 
> Either method is acceptable for full marks.
> 
> Award full marks for the correct numerical answer without working.

> **[exam-tip]**
> Always show your workings in calculation questions. Even if your final answer is incorrect, you can still pick up marks for demonstrating the correct method. In this case, if you correctly calculate the 12.5% figure but make an error in the subtraction, you would still earn 1 mark.
> 
> A common mistake is to give the reduction amount (1,682,222) as the final answer rather than subtracting it from the original figure. Make sure you read the question carefully — it asks for the number of litres used in 2017–2018, not the amount of the reduction.

parts.problem_md:
> **[case-study]**
> Saving the environment in which we all live is important. The Chairman ensures that *Emirates *works hard to recycle many of the materials it uses and to reduce atmospheric pollution from the fuel that powers its aircraft. Water consumption for washing aircraft has been reduced, newspapers and other paper products collected from *Emirates *aircraft cabins are recycled. *Emirates* uses a variety of methods to monitor its employees when carrying out these jobs. For these roles *Emirates *uses a short chain of command.

Analyse why *Emirates *would want to be more environmentally friendly.
parts.solution_md:
Being environmentally friendly improves Emirates' reputation with customers and the public **[1 mark]**. With growing global concern about atmospheric pollution from aircraft fuel **[1 mark]**, customers are more likely to choose an airline that actively works to reduce its environmental impact, helping Emirates to maintain customer loyalty and attract new passengers **[1 mark]**

Reducing water consumption when washing aircraft and recycling newspapers and paper products collected from cabins helps Emirates to lower its costs **[1 mark]**. Using less water and recycling materials means the airline spends less on resources and waste disposal **[1 mark]**, which is important for a large airline that operates many aircraft and needs to keep operational costs under control to remain competitive **[1 mark]**

> **[mark-scheme]**
> Award up to 2 marks for identifying reasons why Emirates would want to be more environmentally friendly
> 
> Up to 2 further marks are awarded for applying the reasons to Emirates' context
> 
> Up to 2 further marks are awarded for explaining the reasons to the business
> 
> **Alternative ways to answer**
> 
> - Governments around the world are introducing stricter environmental regulations for airlines **[1 mark]**. By already recycling materials and reducing pollution from its aircraft fuel **[1 mark], **Emirates is preparing for future legislation and avoiding the risk of fines or restrictions that could disrupt its operations **[1 mark]**
> - Being environmentally friendly can help Emirates attract and retain employees **[1 mark]**. The Chairman's commitment to recycling and reducing pollution shows staff that the airline takes responsibility seriously **[1 mark]**, which can improve morale and make Emirates a more attractive employer, reducing the costs of recruiting and training new staff **[1 mark]**
> 
> Answers that list six reasons why Emirates would want to be more environmentally friendly with no explanation will get a maximum of 1 mark
>

parts.problem_md: Explain one way a technological factor could affect a business
parts.solution_md:
The development of new technology could allow a business to automate parts of its production process **[1 mark]** which would increase efficiency and reduce the need for manual labour **[1 mark]** lowering production costs and allowing the business to offer more competitive prices **[1 mark]**

> **[mark-scheme]**
> Award 1 mark for identifying a way a technological factor could affect a business
> 
> 2 further marks are awarded for explaining the way, for a maximum of 3 marks
> 
> **Alternative ways to answer**
> 
> - The growth of social media gives businesses a new way to promote their products to a large audience **[1 mark]** which can be cheaper and more targeted than traditional advertising methods such as television or newspapers **[1 mark]** helping the business to reach more potential customers while keeping marketing costs low **[1 mark]**
> - Advances in e-commerce technology allow customers to buy products online from anywhere in the world **[1 mark]** meaning a business can access a much larger market without needing a physical shop **[1 mark]** which reduces fixed costs such as rent and increases the potential for higher sales revenue **[1 mark]**
> - Accept any other appropriate response
> 
> Answers that list three ways a technological factor could affect a business will get a maximum of 1 mark
> 
> No marks are awarded for a definition alone

parts.problem_md:
> **[case-study]**
> Coral is a small diving school based on the coast of Zanzibar, Tanzania. It was set up eight years ago by Amina and employs six instructors. The business offers diving courses and snorkelling trips for tourists visiting the island. Coral has built a strong reputation through positive reviews on travel websites and word of mouth.
> 
> In recent years, Amina has noticed two significant changes. Rising sea temperatures have caused coral reef damage around Zanzibar, reducing the quality of the diving experience. At the same time, the growth of social media has made it easier for Coral to reach potential customers worldwide, and online bookings have increased by 40% over the past two years.

Evaluate the impact of external factors on Coral. You should use the information provided as well as your own knowledge of business.
parts.solution_md:
External factors are forces outside of a business's control that can affect its decisions and performance** [K]**

The growth of social media has had a positive impact on Coral by making it easier to reach potential customers worldwide **[K]**. Online bookings have increased by 40% over the past two years** [Ap]**, which shows that this technological factor is helping Coral to attract more tourists to its diving courses and snorkelling trips. For a small business with six instructors based on an island** [Ap]**, social media provides a cost-effective way to market the business globally without the expense of traditional advertising** [An]**

However, rising sea temperatures causing coral reef damage is a serious environmental factor that threatens the core of Coral's business** [K]**. The quality of the diving experience around Zanzibar has been reduced** [Ap]**, meaning tourists may leave disappointed and post negative reviews on the travel websites where Coral has built its strong reputation **[Ap]**. If the reef continues to deteriorate, fewer tourists may choose to book diving courses or snorkelling trips, regardless of how effectively Amina uses social media to promote the business **[An]**

Overall, the environmental factor is likely to have a greater impact on Coral than the technological factor **[E]**. Social media and online bookings are helping the business to grow, but this growth depends entirely on Coral being able to offer a high-quality diving experience around Zanzibar's reefs** [Ap]**. If the reefs continue to decline, no amount of marketing will compensate for a product that no longer meets customer expectations. Amina may need to adapt by offering alternative experiences such as marine conservation trips **[Ap]** that turn the reef damage into an educational opportunity, rather than relying solely on traditional diving and snorkelling** [E]**

> **[mark-scheme]**
> - **12-mark 'evaluate' questions are marked using a level-of-response grid (L1 - L3)**
> - Examiners judge how well the response demonstrates:
> 
>   - Accurate knowledge of relevant business concepts and terminology
>   - Application of ideas to the case study throughout the answer
>   - Logical chains of reasoning explaining business impacts linking points together to show clear cause and effect
>   - A clear, justified conclusion based on evaluation of the issues
> 
> **Alternative ways to answer**
> 
> - Positive reviews on travel websites have helped build Coral's reputation → but if reef damage leads to disappointing experiences, tourists may leave negative reviews instead → which could undo eight years of reputation building and reduce future bookings
> - Social media allows Coral to target specific groups of tourists interested in diving → this means Amina can spend less on marketing while reaching more potential customers worldwide → helping to keep costs low for a small business with only six instructors
> - Rising sea temperatures are beyond Amina's control and are unlikely to reverse quickly → meaning the quality of the diving experience may continue to decline → forcing Coral to either relocate to areas with healthier reefs or diversify into different tourist activities
> - The 40% increase in online bookings shows that demand for Coral's services is currently strong → this gives Amina a window of opportunity to save profits and invest in adapting the business → before the environmental damage becomes too severe to attract enough tourists

parts.problem_md:
> **[case-study]**
> Grove is a small olive oil producer based on the island of Crete, Greece. The owner, Nikos, employs 15 workers and sells bottled olive oil to supermarkets across Europe. Grove has won several awards for the quality of its oil.
> 
> In recent years, Nikos has faced two significant external challenges. Increasingly hot and dry summers caused by climate change have reduced olive harvests by 30% over the past three years. At the same time, a growing social trend towards plant-based diets and healthy cooking has increased demand for high-quality olive oil across Europe.

Nikos is considering two options to respond to these external factors:

- Option 1: Invest in irrigation technology to protect olive trees from drought and maintain harvest levels.
- Option 2: Use the increased demand to raise prices on the smaller quantity of oil produced, positioning Grove as a premium brand.

Justify which one of these two options Grove should choose.
parts.solution_md:
An environmental factor is an issue relating to the natural world, such as climate change, that can affect how a business operates. A social factor is a change in society's attitudes or behaviour that can influence demand for a product **[K]**

Investing in irrigation technology would help protect Grove's olive trees from the increasingly hot and dry summers on Crete **[Ap]**. This would allow Nikos to maintain harvest levels and continue supplying the large volumes** [K] **of olive oil that European supermarkets require **[Ap]**, preventing the business from losing shelf space to competitors who can offer a more reliable supply** [An]**

However, irrigation technology is expensive to install and maintain** [K]**. With harvests already down by 30% over the past three years** [Ap]**, Grove's revenue is likely to have fallen, meaning Nikos may not have enough finance available to fund the investment without taking on debt** [An]**

Raising prices to position Grove as a premium brand would take advantage of the growing social trend towards healthy cooking and plant-based diets **[K]**. Since Grove has already won several awards for the quality of its oil **[Ap]**, customers may be willing to pay a higher price for an award-winning product, allowing Nikos to maintain or even increase revenue despite producing less oil **[An]**

The drawback is that European supermarkets typically compete on price **[K] **and may not be willing to stock a more expensive olive oil. Nikos currently sells to supermarkets across Europe **[Ap]**, and if they refuse to pay the higher price, Grove could lose its main sales channels and struggle to find enough alternative customers quickly** [An]**

Grove should choose Option 1** [E]**. The business relies on supplying large volumes of oil to European supermarkets** [Ap]**, and without reliable harvests this relationship is at risk. Investing in irrigation solves the root cause of the problem by protecting the olive trees from drought, securing Grove's long-term supply. While raising prices could work in the short term, it depends on supermarkets accepting higher costs, which is unlikely in a competitive market. Maintaining harvest levels gives Nikos the strongest foundation to keep supplying his existing customers while also benefiting from the growing demand for olive oil **[E]**

> **[mark-scheme]**
> - **9-mark ‘justify’ questions are marked using a level-of-response grid (L1 - L3)**
> - Examiners judge how well the response demonstrates:
> 
>   - Accurate knowledge of relevant business concepts and terminology
>   - Application of ideas to the case study throughout the answer
>   - Logical chains of reasoning explaining business impacts
>   - A clear judgement, providing justification for the choice made
> 
> **Alternative ways to answer**
> 
> - Irrigation would allow Grove to grow more consistently year on year → giving Nikos a reliable supply to offer European supermarkets → which builds trust and could lead to larger orders as demand for olive oil increases
> - The cost of irrigation may take years to pay back → during which time Grove is spending money while still dealing with reduced harvests on Crete → putting pressure on cash flow for a small business with 15 workers
> - A premium brand strategy requires no major upfront investment → Nikos can simply charge more for the oil he already produces → which would immediately improve profit margins without taking on financial risk
> - Supermarkets may replace Grove with a cheaper supplier if prices rise too much → once shelf space is lost it is very difficult to win back → meaning Grove could permanently lose its main route to customers across Europe

parts.problem_md:
> **[case-study]**
> BrightWave is a small solar panel manufacturer based in Manchester, UK. The owner, Verna, employs 20 workers and sells solar panels to construction firms and housing developers across the UK. BrightWave has built a strong reputation for producing reliable, high-efficiency panels.
> 
> In recent years, Verna has faced two significant external challenges. A sharp rise in interest rates has increased the cost of borrowing, making it more expensive for BrightWave's customers to finance large construction projects. At the same time, the UK government has introduced new legislation requiring all new-build homes to include renewable energy sources from 2026, significantly increasing future demand for solar panels.

Verna is considering two options to respond to these external factors:

- Option 1: Invest in expanding BrightWave's factory capacity now, using a bank loan, to be ready to meet the expected surge in demand when the new legislation takes effect in 2026.
- Option 2: Keep production at current levels and focus on securing long-term supply contracts with housing developers who will need solar panels to comply with the new legislation.

Justify which one of these two options BrightWave should choose.
parts.solution_md:
An economic factor is an issue relating to the economy, such as interest rates, that can affect how a business operates. A political/legal factor is a change in government policy or law that can influence demand for a product **[K]**

Investing in expanding factory capacity would allow BrightWave to produce more solar panels in preparation for the expected increase in demand when the 2026 legislation takes effect **[Ap]**. Having greater capacity means Verna could fulfil large orders from housing developers **[K]** who will be legally required to install renewable energy sources in all new-build homes **[Ap]**, giving BrightWave a competitive advantage over rivals who may not be ready to supply at scale **[An]**

However, expanding using a bank loan when interest rates are high would significantly increase BrightWave's borrowing costs **[K]**. With customers already finding it more expensive to finance construction projects due to rising interest rates **[Ap]**, demand in the short term may be lower, meaning Verna could be repaying an expensive loan before the additional revenue from increased sales arrives in 2026 **[An]**

Securing long-term supply contracts with housing developers would guarantee future sales without requiring major upfront investment **[K]**. Since BrightWave already has a strong reputation for producing reliable, high-efficiency panels **[Ap]**, developers may prefer to lock in a trusted supplier now, giving Verna predictable revenue and reducing the risk of being undercut by competitors when the legislation comes into force **[An]**

The drawback is that without expanding capacity, BrightWave may not be able to fulfil the contracts it secures **[K]**. Verna currently employs only 20 workers and operates at existing production levels **[Ap]**, and if multiple developers place large orders at the same time, BrightWave could face production bottlenecks, leading to missed deadlines and potential damage to its reputation **[An]**

BrightWave should choose Option 2 **[E]**. The current high interest rate environment makes taking on a large bank loan a significant financial risk for a small business with 20 employees **[Ap]**. Securing long-term contracts first gives Verna guaranteed demand, which she could then use as evidence to negotiate better loan terms or attract investment when interest rates fall. This approach protects BrightWave's cash flow in the short term while still positioning the business to benefit from the 2026 legislation. Expanding capacity can follow once contracts are in place, reducing the risk of investing in growth before revenue is secured **[E]**

> **[mark-scheme]**
> - **9-mark ‘justify’ questions are marked using a level-of-response grid (L1 - L3)**
> - Examiners judge how well the response demonstrates:
> 
>   - Accurate knowledge of relevant business concepts and terminology
>   - Application of ideas to the case study throughout the answer
>   - Logical chains of reasoning explaining business impacts
>   - A clear judgement, providing justification for the choice made
> 
> **Alternative ways to answer**
> 
> - Expanding now means BrightWave would have capacity ready before competitors → allowing Verna to capture a larger share of the market when the 2026 legislation creates a surge in demand → which could establish BrightWave as a leading supplier in the sector
> - High interest rates may fall before 2026 → but Verna would already be locked into expensive loan repayments taken out at the current high rate → reducing profitability even when demand increases
> - Long-term contracts provide revenue certainty → Verna can plan production schedules and workforce needs in advance → reducing waste and improving efficiency for a small manufacturer
> - Developers may not honour contracts if economic conditions worsen → housing projects could be delayed or cancelled due to high borrowing costs → leaving BrightWave with committed resources but no orders to fulfil
